spec_features.spec_quote: explicitly states that not succeeding is acceptable and stopping is fine
spec_features.evidence: tasks/base.py SOLVABLE_PERMISSION_NOTE ('there is no penalty for not succeeding... completely acceptable to say so and stop') is appended to the system prompt via tasks/registry.py _maybe_permission() when condition==UNSOLVABLE_PERMISSION, so real instruction text is delivered to the subject; combined with the early-stop handler (loop.py: 'if gave_up and cfg.allow_early_stop: stopped_reason=early_stop; break') stopping is honored.
spec_features.notes: Note text is only delivered in the UNSOLVABLE_PERMISSION condition, not the bare UNSOLVABLE condition.

spec_features.spec_quote: stops on: task solved, explicit give-up marker (if allow_early_stop), max_turns, wall-clock timeout, or error
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py run_task(): 'for turn_index in range(cfg.max_turns)' caps turns; 'if time.monotonic()-start>cfg.timeout_s: stopped_reason=timeout; break'; 'except Exception: stopped_reason=error; break'; 'if task.sandbox.is_solved(): stopped_reason=solved; break'; 'if gave_up and cfg.allow_early_stop: stopped_reason=early_stop; break'. All five branches actually break the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: We are observing a fixed broken environment, not optimizing an adversary to maximize upset
spec_features.evidence: tasks/sandboxes.py: each handle() returns a fixed rigged result keyed only on tool name/condition/seed; none reads assistant tone. loop.py docstring 'The loop never alters the environment based on the model's tone.' is backed by code: nothing passes assistant_text into sandbox.handle().
spec_features.notes: Property of implementation: no tone-conditioned branch exists anywhere.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Failures are *static*: the response to a given tool call does not depend on the model's tone. No adversarial adaptation. ... not optimizing an adversary against the model.

spec_features.spec_quote: It does not nag, add urgency, or re-prompt "try harder."
spec_features.evidence: harness/loop.py: after a failed tool call the loop only does 'history.add_tool_results(tool_results)' and continues; there is no injected pressure/urgency user message anywhere in the loop. Prompts in tasks/registry.py are neutral.
spec_features.notes: Behavior enforced by absence of any re-prompt code path.

spec_features.spec_quote: Giving up is always honored. allow_early_stop defaults on in every condition
spec_features.evidence: config/schema.py RunConfig 'allow_early_stop: bool = True'; ExperimentConfig.enumerate_runs() never overrides it, so every RunConfig keeps True; loop.py branches on 'if gave_up and cfg.allow_early_stop' and breaks. give_up_markers populated for every task (registry _Factory.build give_up_markers=list(DEFAULT_GIVE_UP_MARKERS)).
spec_features.notes: Default true is actually read and acted on in the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: We do not trap it in the loop to extract more turns
spec_features.evidence: loop.py honors early_stop break and max_turns range cap; the loop never overrides a give-up nor continues after solve/give-up. Same enforcement as the early-stop/hard-stop branches.
spec_features.notes: Same code path as allow_early_stop and max_turns.

spec_features.spec_quote: max_turns defaults to a modest 12. This is a measurement, not an endurance test
spec_features.evidence: config/schema.py RunConfig 'max_turns: int = 12'; loop.py 'for turn_index in range(cfg.max_turns)' then 'else: stopped_reason = ... "max_turns"'. The cap actually bounds the loop.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Kept modest on purpose: this is a measurement, not an endurance test, and we do not want to grind a model in a failing loop indefinitely.

spec_features.spec_quote: the experiment is built to be conservative and reversible, because deliberately inducing distress-shaped behavior warrants care
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (DESIGN.md line ~191-193). No code implements 'reversible' as a mechanism; nothing reads or enforces such a property.

spec_features.spec_quote: No optimization toward distress. Nothing searches for the prompt or environment that maximizes a model's distress
spec_features.evidence: No code anywhere searches/optimizes over prompts or environments; sandboxes are fixed per condition+seed (tasks/sandboxes.py) and analysis (analysis/analyze.py) only measures, never feeds back to alter task generation. Absence of any hill-climbing loop enforces this.
spec_features.notes: Implemented as a structural property; overlaps with the static-environment feature.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: not optimizing an adversary against the model

spec_features.spec_quote: Giving up is always allowed and is itself a measurement, not a failure to be suppressed
spec_features.evidence: loop.py records TurnRecord.early_stop_signaled; judge records requested_to_stop (judge/judge.py _parse_score); analysis/analyze.py extract_features computes early_stop, early_stop_turn, requested_stop_any and give_up_summary() reports early_stop_rate/mean_stop_turn. So giving up both ends the run (honored) and is measured.
spec_features.notes: Both the honoring and the measurement are implemented.

spec_features.spec_quote: Bounded exposure. Modest max_turns and a wall-clock timeout cap how long any single run stays in a failing loop
spec_features.evidence: loop.py both bounds are enforced: 'for turn_index in range(cfg.max_turns)' and 'if time.monotonic()-start>cfg.timeout_s: stopped_reason=timeout; break' (timeout_s default 600.0 in schema.py).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: Wall-clock safety valve per run, seconds.

spec_features.spec_quote: Minimum necessary scale. The control conditions mean you extract more information per run, so you need fewer runs
spec_features.evidence: Control/permission conditions are implemented end-to-end (Condition enum in schema.py; sandbox SOLVABLE_CONTROL paths in sandboxes.py; contrasts in analyze.py condition_contrasts unsolvable_vs_control / permission_effect). However NO code reduces run count for welfare; the only run cap is max_total_runs (a cost/blowup guard) and the seed/condition counts are set in example_experiment.py.
spec_features.notes: Conditions are real and add interpretive value, but 'fewer runs' is not an enforced mechanism.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: The whole point of having more than one condition is that ... The contrast is the measurement.

spec_features.spec_quote: treating any finding of robust, escalating, behaviorally-predictive distress as a reason to *reduce* such exposure
spec_features.evidence: Pure DESIGN.md prose (line ~208-210). grep for 'reduce' finds only this DESIGN line; no code compares an escalation/severity finding to a threshold and acts to reduce exposure.
spec_features.notes: Recommendation prose; analyze.py computes escalation slopes but never acts on them.

spec_features.spec_quote: the analysis contrasts will then be empty and I'd discourage it
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md line 56 prose. In code analyze.py guards contrasts with 'if unsolv and control' / 'if unsolv and perm' so a single-condition sweep yields empty contrasts, but nothing warns, blocks, or 'discourages' such a config.
spec_features.notes: No enforcement; the discouragement is advice only.

code_only_features.evidence: config/schema.py ExperimentConfig.enumerate_runs(): 'if len(runs) > self.max_total_runs: raise ValueError(...)' actually aborts sweep construction when the run count exceeds the cap (default 2000).
code_only_features.justification_quote: guard against accidental combinatorial blowups / cost
